Story file: - docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md exists and defines REQ-MAINT-DETECT / UPDATE / BATCH / VERIFY / REPORT / SAFE.
Implementation (core maintenance API and exports): - src/maintenance/index.ts - Exports: detectStaleAnnotations, updateAnnotationReferences, batchUpdateAnnotations, verifyAnnotations, generateMaintenanceReport. - Annotated with @story docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md and all REQ-MAINT-* IDs. - src/index.ts - Imports these maintenance functions and exports them under a maintenance object: - const maintenance = { detectStaleAnnotations, updateAnnotationReferences, batchUpdateAnnotations, verifyAnnotations, generateMaintenanceReport }; - export { rules, configs, maintenance }; export default { rules, configs, maintenance }; - Annotated with @req REQ-MAINTENANCE-API-EXPORT (Story 009), integrating maintenance tools with the primary plugin export. - package.json - "bin": { "traceability-maint": "lib/src/maintenance/cli.js" } ensuring the CLI is available as traceability-maint when the package is installed.
Implementation (detection & verification – REQ-MAINT-DETECT / REQ-MAINT-VERIFY / REQ-MAINT-SAFE): - src/maintenance/detect.ts - detectStaleAnnotations(codebasePath: string): string[] - Resolves a workspaceRoot from process.cwd() and codebasePath. - If workspaceRoot does not exist or is not a directory, returns [] (safe no-op). - Uses getAllFiles(workspaceRoot) from src/maintenance/utils.ts to traverse all files. - Reads each file, parses @story values with regex /@story\s+([^\s]+)/g. - For each storyPath: - isUnsafeStoryPath(storyPath) short-circuits unsafe / traversal / invalid-extension values, skipping any fs checks. - Computes project and codebase candidates and passes them through enforceProjectBoundary (from src/utils/storyReferenceUtils) to ensure paths stay within workspaceRoot. - Only for in-project candidates, calls fs.existsSync; if none exist, adds storyPath to stale set. - Returns a de-duplicated list of stale story paths. - Helper functions (processFileForStaleAnnotations, handleStoryMatch, getInProjectCandidates, anyInProjectCandidateExists) include @story 009 and @req REQ-MAINT-DETECT annotations. - src/maintenance/batch.ts - verifyAnnotations(codebasePath: string): boolean - Calls detectStaleAnnotations and returns stale.length === 0. - Provides verification API for post-maintenance checks (REQ-MAINT-VERIFY). - src/maintenance/utils.ts - getAllFiles(dir: string): string[] and traverseDirectory(...): - Recursively traverse directories; return [] if dir missing or not a directory (safety). - Shared traversal logic for detection and update operations; annotated for Story 009 with REQ-MAINT-UTILS-*.
Implementation (update & batch – REQ-MAINT-UPDATE / REQ-MAINT-BATCH / REQ-MAINT-SAFE): - src/maintenance/update.ts - updateAnnotationReferences(codebasePath, oldPath, newPath): number - If codebasePath does not exist or is not a directory, immediately returns 0 without modifications. - Escapes oldPath for regex and builds /(@story\s*)/g. - Iterates over all files returned by getAllFiles(codebasePath), processes each file with processFileForAnnotationUpdates: - Skips non-regular files. - Reads content, applies regex replacement using a callback that increments a shared count and replaces oldPath with newPath. - Writes the file back only if content changed (preserving formatting in unrelated areas). - Returns the total number of @story annotations updated. - src/maintenance/batch.ts - batchUpdateAnnotations(codebasePath, mappings: { oldPath: string; newPath: string }[]): number - Loops over mappings, invoking updateAnnotationReferences for each and summing counts. - Implements batch updates across multiple paths (REQ-MAINT-BATCH).
Implementation (reporting & safety – REQ-MAINT-REPORT / REQ-MAINT-SAFE): - src/maintenance/report.ts - generateMaintenanceReport(codebasePath): string - Calls detectStaleAnnotations. - If there are no stale annotations, returns "" (empty string) to indicate no actions required. - Otherwise returns a newline-separated list of stale story paths. - Annotated with REQ-MAINT-REPORT and REQ-MAINT-SAFE.
Implementation (CLI UX & error handling – all REQ-MAINT-*): - src/maintenance/cli.ts - runMaintenanceCli(rawArgv: string[]): number - Commands: detect, verify, report, update; unknown commands print error + help and exit with code 2. - Catches unexpected errors, prints concise diagnostic message ("traceability-maint failed: ...") and exits with usage code 2 (REQ-MAINT-SAFE). - Flag parsing: - ParsedFlags: { root, json, format?, from?, to?, dryRun? }. - createDefaultFlags: root defaults to process.cwd(), json false (safe defaults). - applyFlag/parseFlags implement predictable, minimal argument parsing (REQ-MAINT-SAFE). - handleDetect: - Uses parseFlags; calls detectStaleAnnotations(root). - If --json is set, prints JSON { root, stale }. - If not, prints "No stale @story annotations found." when none, or each stale path on its own line plus a summary line that suggests using report. - Returns 0 when stale.length === 0, otherwise 1 (EXIT_STALE). - handleVerify: - Calls verifyAnnotations(root). - If valid, prints "All traceability annotations under are valid." and returns 0. - If not, prints a short guidance message and returns 1. - handleReport: - Calls generateMaintenanceReport(root). - If format=json, prints JSON { root, report }. - Otherwise, prints either "No stale @story annotations found. Nothing to report." or a Markdown-like header and list of stale paths. - Always exits with code 0 (report generation is always considered successful). - handleUpdate: - Validates that both --from and --to are provided; otherwise prints an error, prints help, and exits with code 2 (REQ-MAINT-SAFE). - Dry-run mode: - Does not modify files. - Uses generateMaintenanceReport to estimate potential stale count; prints either JSON or human-readable summary of what would be changed, including estimatedStaleCount. - Exits with 0, clearly stating no changes were made. - Normal mode: - Calls updateAnnotationReferences(root, from, to) and prints either a JSON summary or a human-readable "Updated N @story annotations from 'from' to 'to' under root.". - Exits with 0.
Tests specifically tied to Story 009 (all containing @story docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md): - tests/maintenance/index.test.ts - Verifies that src/maintenance/index.ts exports detectStaleAnnotations, updateAnnotationReferences, batchUpdateAnnotations, verifyAnnotations, generateMaintenanceReport as functions. - @req REQ-MAINT-SAFE ensures module export surface is correct. - tests/maintenance/cli.test.ts - Validates CLI behavior end-to-end: - detect with no stale annotations: exit code 0, logs "No stale @story annotations found.". - verify with valid annotations: makes a temporary workspace with a matching .story.md; exits 0 and logs once. - report: with a missing.story.md annotation, exits 0 and logs a human-readable report containing "Traceability Maintenance Report" and the missing story path. - update: with a file containing @story old.path.md, performs replacement to new.path.md, exits 0 and confirms updated content. - update without --from/--to: exits 2 and ensures both console.error and console.log (help) were called. - update --dry-run: does not modify files, exits 0, and content remains identical to original. - detect --json: with a stale.story.md annotation, exits 1, logs exactly one JSON payload with a stale array that includes "stale.story.md". - Returns empty string when there are no stale annotations. - When a file contains @story non-existent.story.md, report output contains that path. - tests/maintenance/batch.test.ts - batchUpdateAnnotations: - Returns 0 when given an empty mappings list. - verifyAnnotations: - With a valid @story and corresponding .story.md file, verifyAnnotations returns true. - tests/maintenance/update-isolated.test.ts - updateAnnotationReferences isolated behavior: - In a temp workspace with @story old.path.md, function updates to @story new.path.md and returns 1. - When rootDir does not exist, returns 0 (safe no-op). - tests/maintenance/detect-isolated.test.ts - More extensive REQ-MAINT-DETECT and safety testing: - Returns [] when rootDir does not exist. - Detects stale annotations across nested directories, expects two distinct stale paths. - Simulates permission-denied directory and expects detectStaleAnnotations to throw, verifying error surface for callers (CLI handles it defensively). - Security behavior: creates file with @story paths including ../outside-project.story.md, /etc/passwd.story.md, invalid.txt, traversalInside, and legitimate.story.md; spies on fs.existsSync to ensure it is never called with: - The raw malicious values. - Their resolved equivalents outside the workspace. - Confirms that only normalized in-workspace paths (resolved traversalInside and legitimate.story.md) are checked.
Documentation & user experience: - README.md ("Maintenance CLI" section): - Introduces traceability-maint as a CLI for maintaining and auditing @story annotations outside ESLint runs. - Describes commands detect, verify, report, update and their behavior. - Provides concrete usage examples, including: - npx traceability-maint --help - npx traceability-maint detect --root . - npx traceability-maint verify --root . - npx traceability-maint report --root . --format json - npx traceability-maint update --root . --from "docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md" --to "docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FN-ANNOTATIONS.story.md". - user-docs/api-reference.md ("Maintenance API and CLI" section): - Documents programmatic API: - detectStaleAnnotations(rootDir): parameters, return type, behavior (recursive scan, unsafe-path skipping, empty array when rootDir invalid). - updateAnnotationReferences(rootDir, oldPath, newPath): parameters, return type, behavior notes (only @story updated, no-op if rootDir invalid, only write on change). - batchUpdateAnnotations(rootDir, mappings): loops over mappings and sums the number of updated annotations. - verifyAnnotations(rootDir): delegates to detectStaleAnnotations and returns true when no stale annotations found. - generateMaintenanceReport(rootDir): returns newline-separated stale story paths or empty string. - Documents traceability-maint CLI: - Commands detect/verify/report/update, all options (root, json, format, from, to, dry-run), and exit codes (0, 1, 2). - Includes example JSON outputs for detect and update --dry-run. - Explicitly states that tools currently focus on stale story references only, aligning with the current implementation scope.

traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria for 009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS appear to be met: - Core Functionality: detectStaleAnnotations, updateAnnotationReferences, batchUpdateAnnotations, verifyAnnotations, generateMaintenanceReport, and the traceability-maint CLI commands detect/verify/report/update collectively provide detection, updating, batch operations, and verification of @story annotations when story files move or are removed. - Quality Standards: Operations are conservative (directory existence checks, targeted @story-only replacements, writes only on change), preserving code behavior and formatting except for the intended annotation updates. - Integration: Maintenance API is exported from src/index.ts; the CLI is wired via the package.json bin field; documentation shows how to use traceability-maint in typical workflows. This integrates cleanly with the existing plugin and project structure. - User Experience: CLI outputs clear text and JSON messages, has distinct exit codes (0/1/2), and includes a help command plus detailed documentation in README and user-docs. Dry-run mode provides safe previews. - Error Handling: Functions and CLI handle missing roots, permission errors, and unsafe paths gracefully. Tests confirm behavior for non-existent directories, permission-denied directories, and path traversal/absolute-path cases where no unsafe fs checks are performed. - Documentation: README.md and user-docs/api-reference.md both include usage examples, behavior notes, and detailed descriptions of the maintenance API and CLI, aligning with the story’s requirements. Given the implemented code, dedicated tests tied to this story, and comprehensive documentation, the story is fully implemented and validated.
